title: Lulu Raghavan on McDonald's Bottom-Up Research | Conveo
summary: Lulu Raghavan of Landor on bottom-up brand research: how McDonald's built for India, why global brands need local insight, and where data meets intuition.
body_markdown:
What does Lulu Raghavan mean by bottom-up brand research? +


Starting from how people in a market actually live, eat and buy, then building the brand around that. Raghavan contrasts it with taking a global template and asking how to customize it for a new country.


How did McDonald's apply a bottom-up approach in India? +


According to Raghavan, McDonald's studied local food patterns, consumption habits and taste preferences, and even grew vegetables in India. She says the McTikki, a vegetarian McDonald's burger, came out of that work.


What research shaped the Tata.ev brand? +


Raghavan says it was largely traditional research: ethnography, observing shoppers, one-on-one walk-alongs and shop-alongs, plus secondary research, followed by a two-day workshop where strategists picked the insight to build on.


Is brand strategy becoming more data-driven? +


Yes, Raghavan says the art is becoming more of a science, with modeling that links brand choices to consumer behavior and business impact. She still believes marketers need the imagination to choose a path, and worries about over-reliance on data.


What customer truth does Raghavan think the industry resists? +


That the customer can be right. She says marketers sometimes disbelieve what they hear from customers and decide they know better, while the best businesses are built on the notion that the customer is right.
